note: ManagedWebSocket read and wrote the stream without the caller's cancellation token, so a peer that stops sending holds a receive (and its buffers) forever. ReceiveAsyncPrivate behind every ReceiveAsync and SendFrameFallbackAsync behind a contended send are where the token was dropped. Proposed by hand from the IL diff of System.Net.WebSockets.WebSocketProtocol 4.5.2 -> 4.5.3 and the 2.1 servicing commit; the copies inside Kestrel and the shared framework have no record here.
